items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Stumpy. You worked with him in some other bands -- [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, worked with him and Claude too.

ctx.x: You know, we didn't have no money hardly. Scuffling you know. And here comes this guy. And he was real raggedy you know. And we had a chum along named Stump Brady. Stump incidentally is one of the -- was one of the best lead trombone players. He was really great and I hope he still can play anyhow.

He brought this guy around to the room and they had one of those Aubon (PHONETIC) books -- it's a big thing -- it's a book that you learn in that's got all the trombone things -- all the exercises and things that a trombone does. And this guy took -- took Stumpy's horn and played everything in tempo.
All the whole thing just like triple tones, double tones, and everything. And he didn't have no teeth.
